name: Offcut Foundry
description: Partition a patterned enamel workpiece into the requested connected offcuts. Each cut changes the remaining material; a wrong local partition can make the final board impossible, while UNDO provides limited recovery. Solve only from screenshots and visible controls in the task webpage. Do not use code, scripts, Developer Tools, console, debugger, inspector, network, source, DOM, page-state inspection, terminal, shell, address-bar or URL edits, reload/navigation, browser extensions, external applications, hidden state, or unrelated tabs.
natural_language: Hold the pointer down and trace each requested connected silhouette on the stock. Cuts must touch the stock edge or a previous cut; use the single UNDO token if a legal-looking partition is wrong. Leave no waste, then CERTIFY CUTS. Solve only from screenshots and visible controls in the task webpage. Do not use code, scripts, Developer Tools, console, debugger, inspector, network, source, DOM, page-state inspection, terminal, shell, address-bar or URL edits, reload/navigation, browser extensions, external applications, hidden state, or unrelated tabs.

metadata.source_notes: TRW-012 grounds the reversed-Tetris mechanic of cutting requested block shapes from a board with exact no-mistake and no-waste objectives. The patterned enamel foundry, original partitions, cut-list presentation, exposure rule, undo budget, browser surfaces, grading replay and procedural generator are original implementation choices.
metadata.variant_count_kind: seeded connected partitions, palettes, textures and cut-list silhouettes
metadata.notes: No pre-control implementation existed. The current original configuration is assigned L4/Full because it combines six connected pieces, changing exposed material, ambiguous visual marks, and one recovery token. The task is static between input boundaries; live and paused observations therefore use the same single endpoint frame.
